verdictReason: Killed, no structural edge. Google's own appeal tool and free guides already list the evidence documents; one guide says most straightforward suspensions can be self-filed and paid help is mainly worth it for account-level cases, which a $149 template cannot fix. Done-for-you rivals are cheaper or riskless for the buyer (freelance bids avg $120; pay-after-completion agency with a 4.9 rating; plans with no reinstatement fee). Assumption-based pessimistic year-1 profit is about -$3.5k. Unverified: template success rate, ad costs.

answers.question: (1) What free/cheap alternative covers the wedge?
answers.answer: Google runs the appeal itself at no charge through a self-serve tool and publishes the optional document list (registration, licence, tax certificate, utility bills) with the rule that evidence must be uploaded within 60 minutes. Free guides add the checklist: one lists 10-16 documents and says name/address must match character-for-character, one says most straightforward suspensions can be self-filed and that paid help is mainly worth it for account-level suspensions. Google Business Profile Community Product Experts can escalate for manual review at no charge. On the done-for-you side, a freelance posting for combined Ads+GBP reinstatement had 52 bids averaging $120 against a $30-250 budget, an agency plan charges $79/location/month with no reinstatement fee, and a Green Thumb Local listing shows a flat fee with reviewers saying payment was not requested until completion. A generic evidence checklist is therefore free; what remains for sale is done-for-you outcome, already priced at or below $149 or with the risk on the seller.

answers.question: (2) What structural edge exists and who could copy it?
answers.answer: None found. A pack generator uses the owner's own licences, utility bills, signage photos and registrations; it adds no exclusive data, licence, or distribution, and a rival or any free guide can copy a template in an afternoon (several already publish the checklist). 'Cheaper', 'AI-built' and 'under 30 minutes' are not edges. The only potentially compounding asset is a private outcome dataset (which pack content gets which suspension type reinstated), but it needs hundreds of cases and rivals already claim 250+ to 295 recoveries. Reinstatement outcome depends mainly on whether the owner has real proof ('tons of proof their business is legit'), not on packaging. Falsifier: a controlled batch of 30+ real cases where the template pack reinstates at least 85% at $149 with refunds under 10% while free-guide DIY filers do materially worse would show a real packaging effect; no public page shows this.

answers.question: (3) Who demonstrably pays and how much?
answers.answer: Paid demand exists but sits with done-for-you providers. Vendor-reported figures (self-reported, unaudited): Search Scope 295 of 300 recovered at a flat $550 upfront; a DesignRush agency profile claims 250+ successful reinstatements; Green Thumb Local shows a 4.9 rating from 206 reviews with reviewers describing payment only after completion; Reputation Arm $600 flat, Reinstatement Experts $450 on success, Green Thumb $349. The only buyer-side price signal I could read is a Freelancer posting for a Google Ads plus GBP reinstatement: budget $30-250, 52 bids, average bid $120. So the buyer anchor is $120-$350 for a done-for-you outcome; nothing shows anyone paying $149 for a do-it-yourself pack.

answers.question: (4) Legal/platform constraints?
answers.answer: Fully dependent on Google's process: evidence must be uploaded within 60 minutes of filing, duplicate appeals are discouraged, and a BrightLocal article says a new process (EU first) gives a single opportunity to apply for reinstatement, so a failed pack can burn the owner's only shot. Service-area rules (hide the address, no virtual offices, no lead-gen agents) mean some suspended listings are genuinely ineligible and no pack fixes that; locksmith/towing are spam-heavy categories so helping them risks assisting policy-violating listings. The pack must never contain fabricated or borrowed documents. Google charges nothing for reinstatement, so the service is sold against a free official path. No UPL-type regime identified for this service.

answers.question: (5) Year-1 numbers (reference entrant: $350 start, 12 h/week)?
answers.answer: Base: 55 orders (assumption: about 5/month from month 2) x 75% net of refunds/failures x $149 = $6,146 revenue; costs $3,964 (startup $350, tools $360, ads $3,000 at an assumed $250/month, payment fees $254) = about $2.2k profit before about 600 owner hours (roughly $3.5/hour). Pessimistic (price x0.8, volume x0.5, cost x1.5): revenue $2,459, cost $5,946, profit about -$3,488. Every volume, refund-rate and ad-spend input is an assumption: no public source gives conversion or CPC for this niche.

killReasons.reason: The wedge (evidence checklist) is free: Google publishes the document list and a free appeal tool, several free guides give 10-16 document checklists, and one says most straightforward suspensions can be self-filed with paid help mainly worth it for account-level cases. A $149 template targets the buyer least willing to pay and cannot fix the hard cases that do pay.

Price is the only differentiator and it is not an edge: done-for-you alternatives already sit at or below $149 (freelancer bids averaging $120, a plan with no reinstatement fee) or shift risk to the seller (flat fee paid after completion, 4.9 rating); an unreviewed stranger asking $149 upfront for a DIY pack is in the worst trust position.

Reinstatement hinges on the owner's genuine proof and listing eligibility, not on packaging, so a template has no demonstrable success-rate advantage and no data moat; success of templated packs is unproven.
Google's reported move to a single reinstatement opportunity (EU first) raises the cost of a failed pack and refund exposure for an entrant with no case history.
Pessimistic year-1 model (price x0.8, volume x0.5, cost x1.5) is negative (about -$3.5k) and base profit is only about $2.2k for roughly 600 owner hours; inputs are assumptions.

assumptions: Price $149 flat, charged upfront (given in the case file).
Orders: 55 in year 1 (about 5/month from month 2; assumption, no source for conversion or lead volume).
25% of orders end up refunded or unrecoverable (assumption; no public success rate for templated packs).

Costs: startup $350 (reference entrant), tools/hosting/domain $30/month = $360, paid ads $250/month = $3,000 (assumption; CPC for this niche not verified), payment fees 2.9% + $0.30 on all orders = $254 (assumption on standard card rates); total $3,964, excludes owner labour (about 600 h).
Pessimistic: price x0.8 = $119, orders x0.5 = 27.5, revenue $2,459; base cost x1.5 = $5,946; profit about -$3,488.
Pessimistic uses base cost x1.5 (not scaled down with volume) as the conservative reading of the rule.

legalNotes: Google Business Profile reinstatement is free and run through Google's appeal tool; the service sells assistance against a free official path (SVC-02-E7).
Evidence must be genuine; never fabricate, borrow or alter licences, utility bills or registrations. Misrepresentation could harm the client and expose the seller.

Google guidelines exclude virtual offices, mailing-address-only listings and lead-gen agents (D16 and Google guidelines page); a pack cannot legitimately fix an ineligible listing. Locksmith/towing/trade categories are spam-heavy, so reinstating them risks helping policy-violating listings.

Platform dependency: appeal rules, the 60-minute evidence window and the number of attempts change (EU-first single-opportunity process reported by BrightLocal); no contractual protection for the entrant.

The client must grant Business Profile manager access if the entrant files for them; Google's terms for third-party access were not read. No unauthorised-practice-of-law regime identified for this service, but not researched exhaustively.
unverified: Success rate of templated evidence packs; no public source found and none can be established without paid cases.

Green Thumb Local $349 price page, Search Scope $550/295-of-300, Sterling Sky pay-on-success terms, and the Reinstatement Experts ($450) and Reputation Arm ($600) prices: these pages were refused by the fetch tool (permission request unanswered) or not re-read, so those figures stay as scan-1 agent_reported evidence (E1, E2, E3, E6) and were not re-verified.
Fiverr GBP reinstatement gig prices (block.fiverr.com refused; the Fiverr listing fetched showed only citation and local-SEO gigs).
Whether the single-opportunity reinstatement process applies in the US or is EU-only so far (BrightLocal and DBA Platform describe EU first).
CPC or organic reach for 'google business profile suspended' keywords; the web-search budget ran out during the work, so only about 5 search queries were possible.
Vendor review counts and recovery claims are self-reported and unaudited.
nextStep: Drop it unless a public source shows a high-volume, paying segment (account-level or repeat suspensions) that a template-assisted flat-fee service can reinstate profitably.
